definitions.explanation: A humble expression used to state one's own intentions, plans, or opinions in formal or official contexts. Used when the speaker lowers their own position to show respect to the listener.

examples.japanese: ⟦{全力|ぜんりょく}を{尽|つ}くす→全力を尽くす：15728_zenryokuwotsukusu⟧{所存|しょぞん}です。
examples.english: I intend to do my utmost.

examples.japanese: ⟦{今後|こんご}→今後：02808_kongo⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{努力|どりょく}→努力：03490_doryoku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{続|つづ}ける→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧{所存|しょぞん}⟦でございます→でございます：19539_degozaimasu⟧。
examples.english: I intend to continue making efforts going forward.

examples.japanese: ⟦{責任|せきにん}→責任：03298_sekinin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}って→持つ：00478_motsu⟧⟦{対応|たいおう}→対応：02510_taiou⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧まいる{所存|しょぞん}です⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{何卒|なにとぞ}→何卒：19658_nanitozo⟧⟦よろしく→よろしく：01070_yoroshiku⟧⟦お{願|ねが}い→お願い：10299_onegai⟧⟦{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます→申し上げる：01734_moushiageru⟧。
examples.english: I intend to handle this responsibly, so I humbly ask for your continued support.

notes:
REGISTER:
A very formal, humble expression. Used in business correspondence, official speeches, formal apologies, and press conferences. The pattern ～⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧{所存|しょぞん}です (I intend to...) is the standard construction. Even more formal with ⟦でございます→でございます：19539_degozaimasu⟧.

COMMON PATTERNS:
Always refers to the speaker's own intentions (humble/humble-adjacent), never to someone else's. The typical pattern is: [verb dictionary form] + {所存|しょぞん}です.

SIMILAR WORDS:
⟦つもり→つもり：01152_tsumori⟧ expresses intention in everyday speech. {所存|しょぞん} is the formal, humble equivalent and would sound stiff or affected in casual conversation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ～⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧{所存|しょぞん}です: I intend to...
- ～⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧まいる{所存|しょぞん}です: I intend to continue...
- {所存|しょぞん}⟦でございます→でございます：19539_degozaimasu⟧: (very formal) I intend to...
